project.name: rfc-rag
project.description: Local RAG MCP server for RFCs: semantic + full-text search with section-level precision. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build context exclusion list that strips git history, build artifacts, IDE settings, AI agent tooling directories, secrets, CI runners, and MCP runtime state from the image build context, keeping the final image clean and the build cache effective.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Three-stage Docker build that produces a minimal .NET 10 Alpine runtime image for the rfc-rag MCP server: a bare Alpine stage extracts only .csproj files for cache-efficient restore, a .NET SDK stage publishes the RfcRag project in Release mode, and a minimal ASP.NET runtime stage adds krb5-libs for Npgsql and launches RfcRag.dll.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the csproj-extraction trick (filter stage on bare Alpine) so dotnet restore runs against only the project file, maximizing Docker layer cache reuse before the full source COPY. The runtime base image is mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine with krb5-libs to suppress the Npgsql GSSAPI warning on Alpine.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Alpine-based stage that extracts .csproj files from the source tree into /out, enabling cache-friendly dependency restore before the full source copy.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: .NET SDK 10 Alpine stage that restores NuGet dependencies using only the .csproj files, then copies full source and publishes RfcRag in Release mode to /app/rfc-rag.

nodes.name: runtime
nodes.summary: Minimal ASP.NET 10 Alpine runtime stage that installs krb5-libs for Npgsql compatibility, copies the published binary, sets migration and globalization environment variables, and starts the MCP server via RfcRag.dll.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Docker build for the RfcRag application: a filter stage (Alpine) strips unnecessary source files, a build stage (dotnet/sdk:10.0-alpine) restores and publishes the ASP.NET project, and a minimal runtime stage (dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine) runs the resulting RfcRag.dll under a non-root user.
nodes.languageNotes: Three-stage build pattern: a lightweight Alpine filter stage copies only needed source paths, the SDK stage compiles and publishes, and the ASP.NET runtime stage produces a minimal, security-hardened image with apk upgrade and non-root USER.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Alpine-based filter stage that selectively copies only required source subdirectories into /out, reducing the build context passed to the SDK stage.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: SDK build stage that restores NuGet packages for RfcRag.csproj and publishes the application in Release configuration to /app/rfc-rag.

nodes.name: runtime
nodes.summary: Minimal ASP.NET runtime stage that upgrades Alpine packages, copies the published output from the build stage, sets environment variables, runs as a non-root user, and starts the application via dotnet RfcRag.dll.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: Primary CI quality gate that runs on push/PR to master: restores, format-checks, builds, runs unit tests with coverage reporting, executes a Docker smoke test against a pgvector Postgres service, and performs a NuGet vulnerability scan.
nodes.languageNotes: Three-job pipeline: build-and-test → docker-smoke (with pgvector service container) and nuget-vuln-scan run in parallel after the build job succeeds.

nodes.name: build-and-test
nodes.summary: Restores NuGet packages, verifies code formatting, builds the solution with analyzers, runs unit tests (excluding integration), generates HTML/Markdown coverage reports, and posts coverage summary as a sticky PR comment.

nodes.name: docker-smoke
nodes.summary: Builds the Docker image and runs a smoke test verifying the MCP stdio server starts successfully against a live pgvector/pgvector Postgres service container.

nodes.name: nuget-vuln-scan
nodes.summary: Scans all NuGet packages (including transitive) for known vulnerabilities, failing the job if any are found and writing security events to GitHub Security.

nodes.name: codeql.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub CodeQL SAST workflow that analyzes C# source for security vulnerabilities and quality issues on every PR/push to master and daily at 04:00 UTC; results appear in the GitHub Security Code Scanning tab.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a matrix strategy over languages (currently just csharp) so additional languages can be added without structural changes.

nodes.name: dependency-scan.yml
nodes.summary: Standalone NuGet dependency vulnerability scan that fails on Critical/High severity packages and non-blocking advisory check for deprecated packages; uploads the vulnerability report as an artifact.

nodes.name: publish.yml
nodes.summary: Builds and pushes a multi-arch Docker image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) to GHCR on CI success or tag push, includes Trivy vulnerability scan, artifact attestation, and creates a GitHub Release for version tags.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated against fork workflow_run events to prevent privilege escalation from forked PRs; uses OIDC-based attestation for supply chain security.

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: Packs and publishes the rfc-rag .NET global tool to both nuget.org (via OIDC Trusted Publishing, no long-lived API key) and GitHub Packages on version tag push or manual dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses NuGet Trusted Publishing (OIDC) so no long-lived NuGet API key secret is required — requires a one-time Trusted Publishing policy configured on nuget.org.

nodes.name: semgrep-scheduled.yml
nodes.summary: Scheduled daily Semgrep full-repository SAST scan (03:00 UTC) using p/auto, p/secrets, and p/owasp-top-ten rule sets; uploads SARIF results to GitHub Security.

nodes.name: semgrep.yml
nodes.summary: PR and push Semgrep security scan using p/auto, p/secrets, and p/owasp-top-ten rules; uploads SARIF to GitHub Security and posts or updates a sticky bot comment on PRs with pass/fail status.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a JavaScript inline script in github-script to upsert a marker-keyed bot comment on the PR rather than creating duplicate comments on each scan run.

nodes.name: 0001-txt-canonical-xml-fallback.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0001: Establishes that plain-text (.txt) is the canonical RFC source format, with XML used only as a fallback, to keep the ingestion pipeline simple and avoid XML parsing complexity.

nodes.name: 0002-sections-as-retrieval-unit.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0002: Decides that RFC sections (rather than arbitrary token chunks) are the fundamental unit of retrieval, preserving document structure and improving relevance precision.

nodes.name: 0003-single-postgres-hybrid-search.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0003: Commits to a single PostgreSQL instance handling vector storage (via pgvector), full-text search (via tsvector), and RRF fusion, eliminating the need for separate search infrastructure.

nodes.name: 0004-raw-sql-dapper-no-orm.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0004: Chooses hand-written SQL via Dapper over an ORM or Entity Framework, keeping full control over hybrid-search queries and avoiding EF migration complexity.

nodes.name: 0005-embedding-model-dimension-lock-in.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0005: Locks the default embedding model to openai/text-embedding-3-small at 1536 dimensions, documenting that changing the model requires a full re-embedding of all stored RFC sections.

nodes.name: 0006-generation-optional-answering.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0006: Makes LLM-based answer generation an optional layer on top of retrieval, so the server can return raw RFC passages without requiring a generation model at runtime.

nodes.name: 0007-deterministic-first-reranking.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0007: Specifies a deterministic-first reranking strategy using named, configurable signal weights (vector score, BM25 score, section position, RFC recency) before optional neural reranking, ensuring reproducible retrieval results and a measurable quality baseline.

nodes.name: 0008-golden-eval-gates.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0008: Introduces golden evaluation gates — a curated set of query/answer pairs used as CI quality gates to prevent retrieval regressions from being merged undetected.

nodes.name: 0009-errata-local-snapshot.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0009: Decides to ingest RFC errata via a local snapshot file rather than live API calls, making the ingestion pipeline reproducible and resilient to IETF API unavailability.

nodes.name: 0010-vectordata-pure-vector-adapter.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0010: Positions the Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData adapter as an additive pure-vector path, leaving the primary Dapper-based hybrid search unchanged and allowing VectorData to coexist without replacing it.

nodes.name: badfile.txt
nodes.summary: Intentionally malformed test fixture (1 line) used to verify the RFC ingestion pipeline's error handling and resilience when processing corrupt or empty input.

nodes.name: rfc1035.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 1035 (Domain Names — Implementation and Specification) test fixture covering the DNS protocol wire format, message compression, resource record types, and resolver algorithm; used as a large-scale ingestion and search test corpus.
nodes.languageNotes: 3077-line plain-text RFC with dense technical sections on DNS message format, master file format, and resolver algorithm — exercises multi-section chunking logic.

nodes.name: rfc2119.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 2119 (Key Words for Use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels) test fixture defining MUST, SHOULD, MAY and related normative keywords; used to verify that short, dense RFCs are parsed and semantically indexed correctly.
nodes.languageNotes: Short 171-line RFC; serves as a minimal-document boundary test for the chunking and embedding pipeline.

nodes.name: rfc3986.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 3986 (Uniform Resource Identifier — Generic Syntax) test fixture covering URI parsing, component decomposition, path normalization, and reference resolution; provides rich ABNF grammar sections for parser and indexing tests.
nodes.languageNotes: 3419 lines including extensive ABNF grammar definitions and algorithm pseudocode — tests multi-type section parsing in the RAG pipeline.

nodes.name: rfc5234.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 5234 (Augmented BNF for Syntax Specifications — ABNF) test fixture defining the formal grammar notation used throughout IETF standards; exercises the pipeline's ability to index notation-heavy technical documents.
nodes.languageNotes: 899 lines with heavy use of formal grammar rules — validates that rule-heavy sections are chunked and embedded without truncation errors.

nodes.name: rfc5681.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 5681 (TCP Congestion Control) test fixture specifying slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery algorithms; used to test ingestion and semantic search across algorithm-dense networking RFCs.
nodes.languageNotes: 1011 lines of algorithm-heavy prose — exercises precise section-level embedding and retrieval for TCP congestion control queries.

nodes.name: rfc793.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 793 (Transmission Control Protocol) test fixture — the original TCP specification — providing state machine diagrams, segment format definitions, and event processing rules; serves as one of the largest and most structurally diverse test documents.
nodes.languageNotes: 5247-line foundational networking RFC with ASCII state diagrams and pseudo-code segments — exercises the pipeline's handling of mixed content types within a single document.

nodes.name: rfc8174.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 8174 (Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words) test fixture clarifying interpretation of normative keywords in lowercase; a short companion RFC used alongside rfc2119.txt to verify cross-document semantic relationships.

nodes.name: rfc8446.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 8446 (The Transport Layer Security Protocol Version 1.3) test fixture — one of the largest in the batch at 8963 lines — covering handshake protocol, record layer, cipher suites, and key schedule; stress-tests large-document ingestion and vector search recall.
nodes.languageNotes: 8963-line security protocol RFC with complex state machines and cryptographic algorithm descriptions — a primary stress-test document for embedding throughput and search precision.

nodes.name: rfc9000.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 9000 (QUIC: A UDP-Based Multiplexed and Secure Transport) test fixture at 8485 lines covering packet formats, connection lifecycle, flow control, and loss detection; tests the pipeline's handling of a modern, complex transport protocol specification.
nodes.languageNotes: 8485-line RFC with interleaved packet format diagrams and normative algorithm prose — validates that the chunker preserves section context across long documents.

nodes.name: rfc9052.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 9052 (CBOR Object Signing and Encryption — COSE) test fixture covering cryptographic message syntax using CBOR encoding; used to verify indexing of data-format-oriented security RFCs with CDDL schema notation.
nodes.languageNotes: 3603 lines mixing CDDL schema definitions with normative prose — tests schema-notation handling in the text chunking pipeline.

nodes.name: rfc9110.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) test fixture — the largest in the batch at 10785 lines — consolidating HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 semantics including methods, status codes, content negotiation, and authentication; primary large-corpus benchmark for ingestion and full-text search.
nodes.languageNotes: 10785-line RFC — the largest test file in the batch — tests maximum-document-size edge cases for both the chunker and pgvector storage.

nodes.name: rfc9293.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 9293 (Transmission Control Protocol) test fixture — the 2022 update to RFC 793 at 5576 lines — providing a modernized TCP specification; used alongside rfc793.txt to test semantic similarity and cross-version retrieval accuracy.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion to rfc793.txt; having both versions in the corpus tests whether the RAG pipeline can distinguish and correctly rank semantically similar but version-distinct documents.

nodes.name: rfc9999.txt
nodes.summary: Synthetic test RFC fixture (28 lines) with a well-formed but fictional RFC header and minimal content; used for unit testing RFC metadata extraction, header parsing, and edge cases around minimal valid documents.
nodes.languageNotes: Synthetic minimal RFC — verifies that metadata extraction (RFC number, title, author fields) works on a controlled, predictable document.

nodes.name: rfc9998-injection.txt
nodes.summary: Security test fixture (66 lines) designed to probe the RFC ingestion pipeline for prompt injection, SQL injection, and other adversarial inputs embedded within RFC-formatted text; validates that the system sanitizes and safely handles malicious content.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally adversarial RFC-shaped document — critical for validating that the text chunking and embedding pipeline does not execute or leak injected content.

nodes.name: rfc822.txt
nodes.summary: IETF RFC 822 (Standard for the Format of ARPA Internet Text Messages) test fixture at 2901 lines specifying the original email message format including header fields, address syntax, and date formats; exercises the pipeline's handling of foundational email protocol documents.
nodes.languageNotes: 2901-line historic RFC defining ARPA email format — validates that older RFC formatting conventions (pre-1990s style) are correctly parsed and indexed.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what rfc-rag is and why it exists: an MCP server that turns the IETF RFC corpus into a semantic-search and question-answering tool backed by PostgreSQL with pgvector. The README explains the three core MCP capabilities (index, search, ask), the hybrid BM25+vector retrieval strategy, and how to get a local stack running — read this first to build the mental model everything else will fill in.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: Program.cs is the .NET 10 host that assembles the entire application: it registers all subsystem DI extensions, wires the MCP server transport, applies database migrations on startup, and then starts the host. Reading it gives you a complete map of every module — search, indexing, answering, infrastructure — before you dive into any of them.
tour.languageLesson: In .NET 10 minimal hosting, WebApplication.CreateBuilder wires DI, middleware, and hosted services in one call. The call chain of AddXxx extension methods here is itself an architectural index: each extension owns one bounded subsystem and registers exactly what it needs.

tour.title: MCP Tool Surface
tour.description: RfcRagTools.cs and RfcAskTools.cs are the public API of the server — the 11 MCP tool handlers (search_rfc, get_rfc, ask_rfc, index_rfc, normative search, ABNF lookup, TOC, errata, and more) that an AI assistant or human client calls. Each handler is a thin delegation layer that validates input, calls a domain service, and serialises the result to JSON. ToolExceptionFilter.cs wraps every call in a structured error boundary so that tool exceptions become well-formed MCP error responses instead of unhandled crashes.

tour.title: Domain Models
tour.description: Before following data through the pipelines, understand the core record types that flow between layers. RfcSection holds a parsed RFC section with its number, heading, and body. RfcMetadata carries document-level fields (RFC number, title, authors, dates, category). SearchResult wraps a section with a relevance score for the caller. These immutable C# records are the vocabulary shared by parsing, indexing, search, and answering — every subsequent step operates on them.

tour.title: RFC Parsing
tour.description: RfcParser.cs handles plain-text RFC documents (the canonical format per ADR-0001): it extracts section boundaries by detecting numbered headings, pulls ABNF grammar blocks, finds RFC 2119 normative keyword occurrences (MUST, SHOULD, MAY), and reads header metadata. RfcXmlParser.cs does the same for xml2rfc XML-format documents (RFC 7991 schema), which are used as a fallback when the text file is unavailable. Both produce an RfcDocument record — the immutable aggregate of all extracted content — which is the input contract for the indexer.
tour.languageLesson: Both parsers implement a common interface registered by ParsingExtensions.cs. The factory pattern (switching on RfcParserType enum) lets the indexer stay decoupled from format decisions — a classic open/closed principle application in .NET.

tour.title: Indexing Pipeline
tour.description: RfcIndexer.cs orchestrates ingestion of an entire RFC mirror: it resolves source files, computes SHA-256 checksums for incremental change detection (already-indexed unchanged RFCs are skipped), calls the appropriate parser, and then fans sections out to EmbeddingService.cs. EmbeddingService.cs batches section text, calls an IEmbeddingGenerator (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small by default per ADR-0005), applies a semaphore for rate-limiting, and writes the 1536-dimension float vectors alongside the sections into PostgreSQL. IndexingExtensions.cs registers all these services in DI.

tour.title: Database Schema
tour.description: The SQL migrations define the PostgreSQL schema that the entire system is built on. Migration 0001 creates rfc_sections (the central table: 1536-dim pgvector column plus a GIN-indexed tsvector for BM25 full-text search), indexed_rfcs (SHA-256 change tracking), rfc_abnf_blocks, and normative_occurrences. Later migrations extend indexed_rfcs with metadata columns, add the index_manifest table for run auditing, and create the rfc_errata table. The schema is the contract between indexing, search, and all query paths.
tour.languageLesson: SQL migrations here use a custom runner (RfcRagMigrationRunner.cs) that computes SHA-256 checksums of each migration file and records them in a schema_migrations table. This idempotent approach means migrations are safe to re-run and the runner will skip already-applied files while catching tampering with applied files.

tour.title: Migration Runner and DI Wiring
tour.description: RfcRagMigrationRunner.cs runs on application startup: it reads SQL files from the embedded Migrations directory in alphabetical order, checks the schema_migrations table, and applies any pending migrations using PostgreSQL advisory locks to prevent concurrent runs. ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs is the top-level infrastructure wiring — it registers the NpgsqlDataSource with pgvector type mapping, the migration runner, OpenTelemetry tracing, and the trace queue that persists QueryTrace records to disk after each search.

tour.title: Search Pipeline: Query Planning and Repository
tour.description: QueryPlanner.cs is the query parser: it uses regex patterns to detect RFC number filters, section references, and normative keyword intent, producing a QueryPlan record that guides how the search will be executed. SearchRepository.cs is the data layer implementing three search strategies against rfc_sections: lexical (tsvector/tsquery BM25), vector (pgvector cosine similarity), and hybrid (BM25+vector with Reciprocal Rank Fusion). The hybrid mode, documented in ADR-0003, is the default because it outperforms either signal alone.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges two ranked lists without needing score normalisation: each document's RRF score is 1/(rank_in_bm25 + k) + 1/(rank_in_vector + k). This is computed inside PostgreSQL via a single SQL query using CTEs, which ADR-0004 justifies as a reason to use raw SQL over an ORM.

tour.title: Search Pipeline: VectorData Adapter and Orchestration
tour.description: VectorDataSearch.cs wraps a PostgresCollection from Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData to provide an alternative pure-vector path (ADR-0010) — it embeds the query, queries the collection, and returns SearchResults. SearchService.cs is the high-level orchestrator: it calls QueryPlanner, dispatches the right search strategy via the repository or the VectorData adapter, applies deterministic reranking (ADR-0007) using configurable signal weights, and attaches a QueryTrace to the result. SearchExtensions.cs registers all these services in DI.

tour.title: Answering Pipeline
tour.description: AskService.cs orchestrates the full ask flow: it calls SearchService to retrieve evidence sections, then passes them to ContextAssembler.cs which deduplicates, collapses overlapping sections, and ranks them into an EvidencePack. AnswerGenerator.cs sends the EvidencePack as a structured prompt to an IChatClient (any M.E.AI-compatible LLM), parses inline RFC citations from the generated text, and returns a GeneratedAnswer. CitationVerifier.cs then cross-references each cited evidence ID against the pack, flagging hallucinated citations. This layered design means the retrieval path works without the LLM (ADR-0006).

tour.title: Architecture Decision Records
tour.description: The docs/adr/ directory is the reasoning layer of the codebase. ADR-0003 explains why a single PostgreSQL instance handles both vector and full-text search instead of a dedicated vector DB. ADR-0006 explains why LLM generation is an optional layer. ADR-0007 documents the deterministic reranking strategy that makes search results reproducible across runs. Reading these three ADRs explains most of the architectural choices you've seen in the code above.

tour.title: Testing Strategy: Fakes and Unit Tests
tour.description: The tests/Fakes/ directory contains a rich library of hand-crafted test doubles rather than general mocking frameworks. SemanticFakeEmbeddingGenerator.cs is the centrepiece: it produces deterministic keyword-aware embeddings so that queries and documents sharing keywords produce high cosine similarity — this makes vector search testable without any real embedding model. Supporting fakes include FakeSearchService, FakeChatClient, FakeTraceWriter, TrackingEmbeddingGenerator, and MisbehavingEmbeddingGenerator for failure-path coverage. RfcRagToolsTests.cs uses these fakes to unit-test all 38 tool-handler scenarios.
tour.languageLesson: The fake embeddings are computed by hashing each keyword to a reproducible float32 vector component, then summing contributions per keyword. This gives embeddings a real geometric structure — similar text produces similar vectors — while being entirely deterministic and free of network calls.

tour.title: Integration Tests with Postgres Container
tour.description: MediumCorpusFixture.cs uses Testcontainers to spin up a real Postgres instance, applies all migrations, and indexes a medium RFC corpus with SemanticFakeEmbeddingGenerator — all in xUnit's collection fixture so the container is shared across test classes. RfcRagIntegrationTests.cs exercises the complete indexing + search pipeline end-to-end: incremental re-indexing, normative keyword filtering, ABNF extraction, and errata retrieval. RetrievalQualityTests.cs takes this further by measuring hit rate and nDCG against a golden question set, ensuring retrieval quality does not regress.

tour.title: CI/CD and Containerization
tour.description: The Dockerfile uses a three-stage build: a filter stage copies only .csproj files for cache-friendly NuGet restore, a build stage compiles and publishes the .NET app, and a minimal ASP.NET 10 Alpine runtime stage runs it. The GitHub Actions CI pipeline enforces format, build, unit tests, integration tests, a Docker smoke test, NuGet vulnerability scanning, and CodeQL/Semgrep SAST on every push. The Makefile wraps all developer operations — quickstart, test, eval, smoke-test — into single commands, and the publish workflow pushes a multi-arch image to GHCR on release.
tour.languageLesson: The three-stage Dockerfile pattern solves Docker layer cache invalidation: because NuGet restore depends only on .csproj files, that layer is cached until a package changes. The app source code — which changes on every commit — is only copied in the second stage, so a rebuild skips the expensive restore step.
